samples.summary: Text autofit height commit still patches `h` alone, so a rotated text box keeps jumping (#1039) around the new compensation
samples.evidence: `this.options.store.updateElementFrame(slideId, elementId, { h: targetH })` writes a size-only patch. `resizeFrameToSize`'s own doc-comment (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/resize.ts:117) states "Callers that write `w`/`h` on a rotated frame must go through this (or `resizeFrameWorld`) rather than patching size alone." This call site bypasses it. The guard above it only skips when an ANCESTOR has a transform (`!ancestorHasTransform`); the element's OWN `frame.rotation` is never considered, so editing text in a rotated text element and committing still writes a bare `h`, moving every painted point exactly as #1039 describes. Pre-existing, but it is the sibling of the path this diff fixes and leaves the two disagreeing.

samples.summary: `anchoredFramePatch` silently discards a caller-supplied x/y when the patch also carries w/h
samples.evidence: `return { ...patch, x: next.x, y: next.y };` — the spread puts the computed x/y LAST, so any explicit `x`/`y` in `patch` is overwritten by the anchor-compensated value. Today `SizePositionSection` only emits `{w}`, `{h}` or `{rotation}` (size-position-section.tsx:102/118/169) so nothing hits it, but `commitFrame` is a generic `(ids, patch: Partial<Frame>)` entry point; the first caller that sets position and size in one patch (e.g. a future align/fit-to-slide action) will have its position silently ignored. Preserving caller intent would require `x: patch.x ?? next.x`.

samples.summary: `resizeFrameToSize` skips the MIN_SIZE clamp every drag path enforces, and now also displaces x/y for degenerate sizes
samples.evidence: `resizeFrame` clamps both axes to `MIN_SIZE = 1` (resize.ts:53-66) and `resizeFrameWorld` routes through it, so no drag can ever produce w/h < 1. `resizeFrameToSize` passes `w`/`h` straight into `frameAtAnchor` with no clamp, and the panel does no validation: `UnitInput.onBlur` accepts any finite number (`unitToPx(n, unit)`, size-position-section.tsx:277; units.ts:15 has no clamp), so typing `0` or `-2` commits `w = 0` / `w = -384`. Previously such a patch at least left x/y alone; now `anchoredFramePatch` also recomputes x/y from the degenerate width, so a rotated element is both collapsed AND relocated. Searched: resize.ts for MIN_SIZE uses, units.ts, size-position-section.tsx UnitInput commit path, memory.ts updateElementFrame (no size validation there either).

samples.summary: A frame whose `rotation` is absent at runtime now yields NaN x/y (element vanishes / persisted corruption)
samples.evidence: `resizeFrameToSize` computes `Math.cos(start.rotation)` / `Math.sin(start.rotation)` (resize.ts:145-146). `Frame.rotation` is typed as required, but real documents can lack it — `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/shape.ts:1106` defends with `const rot = frame.rotation ?? 0` and `packages/slides/test/view/editor/image-crop-session.test.ts:30` normalises with `frame.rotation ?? 0`, and the Yorkie store hands back raw document data. With `rotation === undefined` both trig calls are NaN, so `next.x`/`next.y` are NaN and the patch writes NaN x/y into the store — before this change a `{w}` patch never touched x/y and was immune. Defaulting to 0 (`start.rotation ?? 0`) or an early return would remove the hazard.

samples.summary: Compensation is computed from the memoised (possibly stale) selection snapshot, which can write x/y consistent with a frame that no longer exists
samples.evidence: `const el = elements.find((e) => e.id === id)` reads `selection.elements`, a snapshot captured by the `useMemo` at index.tsx:91 and refreshed only when `tick` bumps (`store.onChange?.(...)`, index.tsx:80 — note the optional call). Size-only patches used to be idempotent under staleness; now a stale `el.frame` feeds `resizeFrameToSize`, which mixes the stale `w`/`h` with the fresh patch axis and produces x/y for a frame that was already superseded (e.g. commit W, then commit H before a re-render: the H patch's x/y is solved with the OLD width while the store holds the new one, shifting the element). Both slides stores do implement `onChange` (memory.ts:1778) and React flushes the state update between events, so this needs an unusual ordering or an `onChange`-less store to fire — hence low confidence, but the new code is the only reason staleness now matters.

finding.summary: Text autofit height commit still patches `h` alone, so a rotated text box keeps jumping (#1039) around the new compensation
finding.evidence: `this.options.store.updateElementFrame(slideId, elementId, { h: targetH })` writes a size-only patch. `resizeFrameToSize`'s own doc-comment (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/resize.ts:117) states "Callers that write `w`/`h` on a rotated frame must go through this (or `resizeFrameWorld`) rather than patching size alone." Pre-existing, but it is the sibling of the path this diff fixes and leaves the two disagreeing.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. editor.ts:4420 writes `updateElementFrame(slideId, elementId, { h: targetH })` — a size-only patch — and the only gate (editor.ts:4294-4297) compares world vs local w/h/rotation, which is identically equal for a top-level rotated text element, so the element's own `frame.rotation` is never considered. resize.ts:108-124 documents that holding x/y fixed across a size change on a rotated frame "moves every painted point" and that such callers must route through `resizeFrameToSize`/`resizeFrameWorld`; this site does not. The store applies the patch verbatim with no rotation compensation (memory.ts:691-708). The path is reachable: `enterEditMode` (editor.ts:4197-4235) and the dblclick dispatcher (editor.ts:4191-4194) impose rotation guards only on tables (editor.ts:4166, 7579), never on text, and text mounts with `growMode: 'auto'` (editor.ts:4356) so `lastEditingContentHeight` is populated (editor.ts:4388-4398). Result: editing a rotated text box whose content height changes commits a bare `h`, shifting the painted geometry — a real incorrect state update on a normally reachable path. No guard, absence, or scope ground refutes it.
